programmes.d: Peter tries to improve his social skills by imitating celebrities.
The Bradys are cast for a laundry soap commercial.
Peter eavesdrops on his family by using a tape recorder.
Jan tries to prove her worth by trying out for cheerleading.
Greg cracks a rib while trying out for the football team.
After yet another rejection of Donald's unpublished novel, Ann offers to submit it to her father, who knows a publisher who's a customer at his restaurant.
Donald does a news story on computer dating and takes Ann along for the ride. Much to Ann's chagrin, the girl that the computer dating service assigns to her boyfriend is a lot like her.
Donald gets Ann to house-sit at his apartment, and she runs into another friend of his (Bill Bixby), who is also staying there.
Before Ann goes to Philadelphia for a play that's making a nationwide tour, Donald tries to show her a good time by giving her a night on the town...and another night...and another night...
Unable to tolerate life without Ann, Donald goes to Philadelphia to write a review of Ann's play.
Donald writes an article on a newfangled psychological exam, and he tries to use it on Ann and the Baumans.
When Oscar learns the park where he and his cronies played baseball is going to be the site for an office building, Oscar becomes civic-minded and decides to run for city councilman.

Singer-composer Paul Williams is the special guest star in this episode written especially for him. Felix Unger's daughter has a crush on Williams and runs away from home to follow him wherever he appears.
Felix discovers that his father and Oscar's knew each other in the old days and that Oscar's father was responsible for Felix's father's downfall.
Oscar Madison takes a job as a sports radio talk-show host but doesn't tell anyone until he finds out whether the station is going to make it permanent.
Oscar Madison falls in love with a beautiful woman who has two children he adores and before he knows it, he's engaged to be married and Felix prepares to lose a roommate.
Greg and Marcia use their dates to get back at each other; the younger Brady siblings prepare for the school carnival by building a dunking tank.

Mike and Carol receive disturbing news of an eyewitness account that Jan stole someone else's bicycle from the park.

Bobby and Cindy are asked by their older siblings to stay out of their way, then are told they weren't invited to their Aunt Gertrude's wedding. In a fit of self-importance, they set out to set a world's record for teeter-tottering.

Bobby develops a Napoleon complex, especially after Greg has to save him from a situation caused in part because he ended up doing something he wasn't supposed to since he was too small to handle the job.
Greg loses a bet to Bobby and has to be his slave for a week.
Peter writes a newspaper column to win points with his teacher.
Alice’s tough-as-nails cousin fills in while she is out of town.
Ann and Donald decide to work on a play about her life, but creative differences get in the way.
An Italian movie director spots Ann and wants her to star in his next movie...and perform a nude scene.
Ann struggles to cook everybody's favorite dishes for a Thanksgiving dinner.
A substitute agent sets Ann up on a publicity date with Dick Shawn, who knows nothing about it.
Originally doubting the intentions of a photographer, Ann is convinced, thanks to Donald, that she should take a job as a model for him because he's legitimate.

Felix has a big commission riding on a new diet pill promotion but the model, "the fattest man in the world," suddenly decides he won't take the job. So Felix convinces Oscar Madison to put on a "fat suit" and pose in the "before" photograph.
When Oscar Madison finds a friend with inside information on his favorite sport, horse racing, he begins to win every bet.

Felix Unger is irate when given notice of another rent increase and organizes the entire building to go on strike until certain repairs and improvements are made to either justify the increase or cancel it altogether.
A pro hockey player hits Oscar and Felix, trying to patch things up, winds up challenging the athlete to a boxing match.
Over Oscar's objections, Felix recounts to their dates how they met while serving on a jury.
